pages.text: Every citizen has $(thing)needs$(0), and a class entry lists what its members expect: a $(thing)home$(0) built for that class, $(thing)food$(0) and $(thing)drink$(0), $(thing)clothing$(0), a heat source and good light, visits to places like the tavern, and $(thing)rites$(0) held nearby. Higher classes add finer foods, aged drinks, jewels, silk, books, pets and even electricity.$(br2)Most of these are goods $(thing)you$(0) must produce and stock.

A satisfied citizen is content, and a content citizen can rise when it aspires to the next path. A citizen whose basics go neglected, such as home, drink or food, slides back down a class.$(br2)Raise the comforts of your base first. Elites and leaders ask for a great deal, and they are only worth having if your economy can keep them supplied.

Some things take care of themselves and are not repeated in each class entry: the $(thing)climate$(0) a culture needs (shown on its overview), sleep, chatting with neighbours, and idle pastimes.$(br2)A few pleasures give a lift without ever being required: music, festivals, the sound of bells, a feeling of homeland.
